results.title: Large prospective investigation of meat intake, related mutagens, and risk of renal cell carcinoma.
results.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
results.reason: Prospective cohort study reporting multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios for dietary heme iron intake and incidence of renal cell carcinoma.

extraction.population: NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study subcohort

sample_size.excerpt: After the exclusions, the baseline analytic cohort included 492,186 ( n = 293,466 men and 198,720 women) participants. The analysis of compounds in cooked and processed meats was restricted to a subcohort that responded to the second questionnaire and met the inclusion criteria above ( n = 302,162; 176,179 men and 125,983 women).

cases.excerpt: Over a mean follow-up of 9 y, we ascertained 1814 cases of RCC ( n = 498 clear cell; n = 115 papillary cell; n = 1071 NOS; n = 147 otherwise specified) in the baseline analysis and 1,089 cases of RCC ( n = 306 clear cell; n = 83 papillary cell; n = 617 NOS; n = 90, otherwise specified) in the subcohort analysis.

confidence_interval.excerpt: For participants in the highest compared with the lowest quintiles of total red meat intake, we observed a tendency toward an increased risk of total RCC (HR: 1.19; 95% CI: 1.01, 1.40; P -trend = 0.06).

p_value.excerpt: We observed a positive trend for heme iron intake and total RCC ( P -trend = 0.03)

results.title: Dairy Product Consumption and Bladder Cancer Risk in the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian (PLCO) Cohort.
results.reason: The study is a prospective cohort investigation of dietary yogurt consumption and incident bladder cancer risk with fully adjusted hazard ratios reported.

extraction.population: Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian (PLCO) Cancer Screening Trial participants
extraction.smoking_status: All smoking statuses included (never, former, current)

sample_size.excerpt: After a median of 12.5 years of follow-up, 776 new cases of bladder cancer were identified from the 101,721 individuals included in our study. Cases were older, were more often men, and were more likely to be current smokers or ex-smokers.

cases.excerpt: Cases ( n = 776)

design.excerpt: In a cohort of 101,721 subjects in the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian (PLCO) Cancer Screening Trial, we analyzed the effects of dairy product intake on bladder cancer risk using Cox proportional hazards regression.

timing.excerpt: Strengths of the PLCO study included the prospective design, large sample size, and high completeness of follow-up, which minimized the selection bias.

continent.excerpt: Briefly, 154,952 individuals aged 55–74 years were recruited via 10 centers in the United States between 1993 and 2001.
continent.location: Materials and Methods, Data Sources, paragraph 1

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Dietary data were collected using the DHQ ( 14 ), which included the portion size and frequency of intake of 124 food items and supplement use during the past year.

confidence_interval.excerpt: There was strong evidence for a substantial association between alcohol intake and risk of upper aero-digestive cancers (oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma, oral cavity, pharynx and larynx; RR per 1 drink/day = 1.38 [95% CI 1.31–1.46]). results.title: Anti-Inflammatory Diet Index and risk of renal cell carcinoma.
results.reason: Prospective cohort study evaluating the association between an anti-inflammatory diet index and incident renal cell carcinoma.

extraction.population: Swedish Mammography Cohort and Cohort of Swedish Men

sample_size.excerpt: Among 71,421 participants, 431 RCC cases were identified during a 19.7-year follow-up.

cases.excerpt: Among 71,421 participants, 431 RCC cases were identified during a 19.7-year follow-up.

effect_size.excerpt: Higher AIDI scores were associated with a lower RCC risk (HR for Q4 vs. Q1: 0.68, CI: 0.52–0.89).

confidence_interval.excerpt: The associations were slightly attenuated but remained significant when using baseline AIDI (1997), with HRs between 0.59 (95% CI: 0.45–0.77) and 0.68 (95% CI: 0.52–0.89).

p_value.excerpt: The most substantial reduction was seen in the highest AIDI quartile (HR: 0.26, 95% CI: 0.11, 0.63), with a p-value for trend at 0.02.

comparison.excerpt: Compared with individuals in the lowest quintile of AIDI (Q1, score 0–5), those in the highest quintile (Q4, score 8–14) had a 31–43% lower risk of RCC
comparison.location: Results / AIDI and RCC incidence, paragraph 1

results.title: Iron Status, Erythropoietin, and Cancer Incidence in the General Population.
results.reason: Prospective cohort study reporting multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios for serum ferritin tertiles and incident kidney cancer.

extraction.population: Community-dwelling individuals in the PREVEND cohort

sample_size.excerpt: Data were obtained from 6109 participants (mean age 52 ± 12 years; 49% male) in the Prevention of Renal and Vascular End‐stage Disease (PREVEND) cohort.

effect_size.excerpt: When looking at site‐specific cancer risk, the relationship between kidney cancer and log‐transformed ferritin (as a continuous variable) remained significant (HR: 0.37, 95% CI: 0.2–0.67; p = 0.005), whereas the previously identified associations were not found to be statistically significant after adjusting for multiple testing.
effect_size.location: Results, Iron Status, EPO Levels, and Site‐Specific Cancer Risk, paragraph 2

confidence_interval.excerpt: When looking at site‐specific cancer risk, the relationship between kidney cancer and log‐transformed ferritin (as a continuous variable) remained significant (HR: 0.37, 95% CI: 0.2–0.67; p = 0.005), whereas the previously identified associations were not found to be statistically significant after adjusting for multiple testing.
confidence_interval.location: Results, Iron Status, EPO Levels, and Site‐Specific Cancer Risk, paragraph 2

p_value.excerpt: Among non‐smokers, elevated sTfR levels were linked to increased cancer risk (HR, 1.68; 95% CI: 1.21–2.32; p = 0.002), a pattern not observed in smokers (HR, 0.81; 95% CI: 0.47–1.39; p = 0.5).
p_value.location: Results, Iron Status, EPO Levels, and Site‐Specific Cancer Risk, paragraph 2

comparison.excerpt: as compared to the lowest tertile of ferritin
comparison.location: Results, Iron Status, EPO Levels, and Site‐Specific Cancer Risk, paragraph 2

results.title: Meat intake, 'mate' drinking and renal cell cancer in Uruguay: a case-control study.
results.reason: This hospital-based case-control study provides multivariable-adjusted odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals for the association between red meat intake and renal cell carcinoma risk.

extraction.population: Patients admitted to the Instituto Nacional de Oncologia in Montevideo, Uruguay

cases.excerpt: This led to a final total of 121 cases and 243 controls.

design.excerpt: In the period January 1988-December 1995, a case-control study of diet and renal cell carcinoma (RCC) risk involving 121 cases and 243 hospitalized controls was carried out in Montevideo, Uruguay.

timing.excerpt: From January 1988. all patients admitted to the Instituto Nacional de Oncologia were routinely interviewed shortly after admittance

exposure_measurement.excerpt: The food frequency questionnaire was short and focused on meat intake. As poultry and fish are infrequently consumed in Uruguay. no infor- mation about these items was collected.

smoking_status.excerpt: Adjusted for age, sex, residence, urban-rural status, education, body mass index and 'mate' drinking.
